questions.stem: You are examining the hands of Ms Little, a 35-year-old hairdresser, with her hands resting on a pillow in the rheumatology clinic. Her knuckles look puffy and she says they are tender. Which manoeuvre is the quickest screen for synovitis across all of her MCP joints at once?
options: Phalen's test: hold both wrists in full flexion for 60 seconds
Prayer sign: press the palms together with the wrists extended
Gently squeeze the 2nd to 5th MCP joints together from the sides
Finkelstein's test: ulnar deviate the wrist with the thumb in a fist
questions.why: The MCP squeeze test is gentle sideways compression across the 2nd to 5th metacarpal heads. Pain on squeezing suggests MCP synovitis and is a useful early sign of RA, often present before any deformity. Ask about pain first and watch her face while you squeeze.
notes: Phalen's test checks for median nerve compression in the carpal tunnel. It does not test for MCP synovitis.
The prayer sign looks at wrist extension and flexor tendon or joint restriction, not at the MCP joints.
Finkelstein's test is for de Quervain's tenosynovitis of the first dorsal compartment, not for MCP synovitis.

questions.stem: The consultant agrees that Ms Little, 35, has seropositive, erosive RA and wants to start methotrexate. Her GP bloods include FBC, UEC, LFT, CRP, ESR, RF, anti-CCP and ANA. Along with a chest X-ray and a pregnancy test, which further test is needed before her first dose?
questions.why: Before starting methotrexate (or any DMARD), check hepatitis B and C serology, because immunosuppression can reactivate hepatitis B and methotrexate is hepatotoxic. A chest X-ray, a pregnancy test and baseline FBC, UEC and LFT are also needed.
notes: HLA-B27 helps when axial spondyloarthritis is suspected. It does not change the methotrexate work-up, and she has no back pain.
Her ANA is negative and nothing suggests SLE, so anti-dsDNA adds nothing before starting methotrexate.
Serum urate is for suspected gout. She has symmetrical RA with no tophi or acute monoarthritis, and urate is not a methotrexate pre-treatment test.

questions.stem: Ms Little, 35, has 3 months of active RA. Her Hb is 112 g/L with an MCV of 84 fL, platelets are 432 × 10^9/L and CRP is 24 mg/L. Her eGFR is above 90 and her LFTs are normal. Which mechanism best explains her anaemia?
options: Warm IgG autoantibodies causing extravascular haemolysis
Low renal erythropoietin output from chronic interstitial nephritis with nephron loss
Vitamin B12 malabsorption from autoimmune gastritis
IL-6 raises hepcidin, which blocks ferroportin and traps iron in stores
questions.why: This is anaemia of chronic disease. Inflammatory IL-6 makes the liver produce more hepcidin, which breaks down ferroportin, so iron stays locked in macrophages and enterocytes and red cell production slows. The result is a mild normocytic anaemia that tracks with disease activity.
notes: Autoimmune haemolysis is more a feature of SLE than RA. She has a negative ANA and no evidence of haemolysis.
Her eGFR is above 90 with normal electrolytes, so a lack of erythropoietin from kidney disease does not fit.
Pernicious anaemia causes a macrocytic anaemia, but her MCV is a normal 84 fL.

questions.stem: Ms Little, 35, has active wrist synovitis from RA and asks why you tested for carpal tunnel syndrome. If flexor tenosynovitis compressed her median nerve within the carpal tunnel, which sensory pattern would you expect?
options: Palmar thumb, index, middle and radial half of ring finger, including the thenar skin
Palmar thumb, index, middle and radial half of ring finger, sparing the thenar skin
Little finger and the ulnar half of the ring finger, front and back
Dorsum of the first web space between the thumb and index finger
questions.why: The palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve leaves the nerve above the flexor retinaculum and runs superficial to it, so the skin over the thenar eminence keeps its feeling in carpal tunnel syndrome. Sensory loss affects the palmar thumb, index finger, middle finger and radial half of the ring finger.
notes: Loss of feeling over the thenar skin points to a median nerve lesion above the wrist, because the palmar cutaneous branch runs outside the carpal tunnel.
This is ulnar nerve territory (compression at Guyon's canal or the elbow), not the median nerve.
The dorsum of the first web space is supplied by the superficial branch of the radial nerve.
